response_text:
Looking at this PR carefully, I need to evaluate the changes across controllers, models, views, specs, and templates.

Key issues I found:

1. **Pagination math bug in `totalPages`** - The formula `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` returns 2 for exactly 50 users with limit=50, but there's only 1 page. Should be `Math.ceil`.

2. **Template scope bug in `group_member.hbs`** - The `{{#unless automatic}}` evaluates `member.automatic` (a User attribute that is undefined), not `group.automatic`. The remove (×) button will always render, even for automatic groups where it must not be shown.

3. **JSON boolean comparison** - `params[:visible] == "true"` won't match a JSON boolean `true` sent by `Discourse.ajax`. Both `update` and `create` actions have this issue, so toggling visibility from the admin UI will not persist.

4. **Spec uses wrong HTTP verb** - The new test for "cannot remove members from automatic groups" uses `:put`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Inconsistent with both the route and the second test in the same context.

5. **Spec coverage gaps** - The rewritten specs only cover the `name` part of `update` (no `alias_level`, no successful rename), and don't exercise search/filter on `index`, nor validation feedback for invalid usernames/user_ids in `add_members`/`remove_member`.

findings.title: totalPages math is off by one for exact multiples
findings.body: totalPages returns Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which yields 2 for user_count=50 with limit=50, 3 for 100 users with limit=50, etc. For exact multiples the result should be (50/50), (100/50)=2, etc. The correct formula is Math.ceil(user_count / limit). With the current code the pagination label displays e.g. "1/2" for a group that actually has only one page, and showingLast becomes true only after stepping into a non-existent page. Consequence: users see an extra phantom page and may be unable to reach later real pages on groups where the count happens to be a multiple of limit.

findings.title: {{#unless automatic}} resolves to member.automatic instead of group.automatic
findings.body: The template is rendered inside `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, so `this` is the iterated User record. `{{#unless automatic}}` therefore evaluates `member.automatic`, which is undefined (User has no `automatic` attribute). The remove (×) button therefore appears for every member, including members of automatic groups, where the controller already forbids removal (remove_member returns 422 for automatic groups). The intended behaviour is to hide the remove link when the surrounding Group is automatic. The render context needs to expose group.automatic (e.g. via the itemView controller, a property pushed onto each member, or by checking the parent controller).

findings.title: params[:visible] == "true" breaks when the client sends a JSON boolean
findings.body: The admin UI sends `visible: !!this.get('visible')` via Discourse.ajax (JSON body), so Rails parses it to a boolean `true`/`false` rather than the string "true". `true == "true"` and `false == "true"` are both false in Ruby, so the assignment becomes `group.visible = false` regardless of what the checkbox shows. As a result the visibility checkbox in the group admin form does not stick. The same pattern appears in `create` on line 25. Use a comparison that handles both, e.g. `ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(params[:visible])` or `params[:visible].to_s == "true"`.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb (PUT instead of DELETE)
findings.body: The new route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (see config/routes.rb), but this test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`. The companion test in the same context (line 125) correctly uses `:delete`. The test as written does not actually exercise the DELETE route; if someone later changed the route to PUT it would still pass and silently break the real endpoint. Change to `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` to match the route.

findings.title: update action is under-tested after the refactor
findings.body: The new `.update` context only covers one scenario: an automatic group ignoring a rename. It does not test that a non-automatic group can be renamed, that alias_level is updated from params[:alias_level], or that the new model asJSON contract (no `group:` wrapper, no `usernames`) round-trips correctly. The renamed `update` no longer touches usernames, so a regression in that decoupling would not be caught.

findings.title: add_members silently drops unknown usernames with no error to the caller
findings.body: `User.find_by_username(username)` returns nil for unknown names and the entry is skipped without feedback. The endpoint always renders success_json even when every requested username was invalid, so the admin UI has no way to surface a partial failure. Consider returning 422 with the list of unresolved usernames when at least one is not found.

findings.title: addMembers does not clear the usernames input after submit
findings.body: After a successful add the controller leaves `usernames` populated (a TODO comment on the line acknowledges this). `model.addMembers` does not reset it either. Clicking Add a second time re-submits the same string and re-issues a PUT for users already in the group, which the controller treats as a no-op but still triggers an extra AJAX round-trip and a full member-list reload.
